**Explanation of the words:**

﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾: that is, time (dahr) in its entirety.

﴿إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ﴾: that is, the whole human kind.

﴿لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾: that is, in decrease and loss, for his life is his capital; so if he dies without having believed and without having done righteous deeds, he has lost with a complete loss.

﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ﴾: that is, they enjoined one another to believe in the truth, to speak it, and to act upon it.

﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾: that is, they enjoined one another to patience in holding to the truth, in speaking it, and in acting upon it.

**Meaning of the verses:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾. These three verses contain a ruling, the one ruled upon, and that which is ruled. The ruling is what Allah the Exalted has judged concerning man, all of mankind, of decrease and loss. The one ruled upon is man, the son of Adam. That which is ruled is loss for whoever does not believe and does not do righteous deeds, and profit and deliverance from loss for those who believe, do righteous deeds, enjoin one another to the truth, and enjoin one another to patience.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾ is an oath which Allah swore. Al-'Asr is time in its entirety: its night and its day, its morning and its evening. The answer to the oath is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾, that is, in decrease, ruin, and loss, since he lives in hardship and dies to go to Jahannam (Hell), so he loses everything, even his own self which is between his sides.

His saying ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾: these are the ones Allah the Exalted excepted from loss, so they are the profiting, not the losing, and that is by their entering Paradise, the abode of happiness. What is meant by faith is faith in Allah and His Messenger and in what His Messenger brought of guidance and the religion of truth. What is meant by righteous deeds is the obligatory acts, the sunan (established practices of the Prophet), and the voluntary acts.

His saying ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ means: to believe in it, to speak it, and to act upon it, and that is by following the Book and the Sunnah.

His saying ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ means: they enjoined one another to the truth in belief, speech, and action, and to patience in that until one of them dies while he believes in the truth, speaks it, and acts according to what it contains. For Islam is true, the Book is true, and the Messenger is true; so by that they believe, act, and enjoin one another to remain steadfast upon it until death.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of the verses:

1. The excellence of Surat al-'Asr, since in three verses it contains the path of deliverance, so much so that Imam al-Shafi'i said: "If Allah the Exalted had sent down to His creation no proof except this surah, it would have sufficed them."

2. An explanation of the destiny of the disbelieving human being, which is complete loss.

3. An explanation of the success of the people of faith and righteous deeds, who avoid shirk (associating partners with Allah) and acts of disobedience.

4. The obligation of enjoining one another to the truth and enjoining one another to patience among the Muslims.
